# Current State

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/docs:3.0 -->

## Verified State

<!-- doc-role:verified-state -->

DeleLuz controls the stock LEDDMX-03 from a native Android app (`app/`, published as [GitHub release v1.1.0](https://github.com/LCubero/deleluz/releases/tag/v1.1.0)) and from Android Chrome (`webapp/`). See [the protocol](../PROTOCOL.md), [the capability table](../CAPABILITIES.md), and the [lab log](../../odd/tasks/led-lab.md) for verified controls and limitations. Linux BlueZ can connect directly to the strip, while the Windows Bluetooth stack fails during characteristic discovery. This does not block building an Android app on Windows: the phone handles BLE.

## Recent Completed Work

<!-- doc-role:recent-work -->

- Published [v1.2.0](https://github.com/LCubero/deleluz/releases/tag/v1.2.0) (build 2015) on 2026-11-26 after the Android UI audit: scene runtime labels and selection, Spanish effect names, and layout fixes, with refreshed screenshots and showreel. See the [audit log](../../odd/tasks/app-ui-audit.md#log).
- RH-W-0001 (Android phase 1) shipped as v1.1.0 (build 2013) on 2026-11-25. The owner approved test build 2012; the automated matrix covered 16 phone sizes. See [roadmap evidence](roadmap.md#resolved-records).
- Published the native Android app v1.0.0 (one universal APK, `DeleLuz-1.0.0.apk`) on GitHub Releases; built on branch `feat/android-app`, merged to `main`, verified by the user on two phones and two strips; independent review and native risk reviews done (`odd/tasks/deleluz-android.md` L41-L56).
- Added onboard-mic sensitivity to the webapp, verified on the strip by the user (`335d91c`; lab L59).
- Recorded Linux BLE connection behavior, power-source observations, and GATT discovery (lab L55–L60).

## Pending Work

<!-- doc-role:pending-work -->

The [Samsung Galaxy A73 5G limit](../../app/README.md#limits) remains: DeleLuz and the vendor app could not connect to the tested LEDDMX-03 (Bluetooth link-layer failure).

The webapp port and two-strip spike await the owner's choice. See the [roadmap](roadmap.md). Full firmware readout and a strip-side timer remain unconfirmed and do not block the Android app.

## Next Step

<!-- doc-role:next-step -->

After v1.2.0 is published, the owner chooses the next phase from [the plan](../PLAN.md): the webapp port (RH-W-0003) or the two-strip spike (RH-W-0002). Get explicit owner approval in the current turn before testing on a physical phone or strip. Announce what each visual strip command will do and wait for the owner's go-ahead before sending it; connecting or retrying does not authorize playback ([audit log](../../odd/tasks/app-ui-audit.md#log), L19).
